title: On one Canary Island, people can whistle Spanish across valleys
body: Silbo Gomero is a whistled form of Spanish from La Gomera, an island whose deep ravines made walking to the neighbors slow. Whistlers turn the sounds of speech into shifting pitches loud enough to carry up to about five kilometers. Its roots likely go back to the island’s original Guanche inhabitants. After decades of decline, it became a compulsory school subject in 1999 and was recognized by UNESCO in 2009.

slides.question: How far can a Silbo Gomero whistle carry?
slides.explanation: Up to about five kilometers, far enough to cross La Gomera’s deep ravines, which made walking to the neighbors slow.

steps.label: Words are split into vowels and consonants
Each sound becomes a whistle, high or low
Pitch and breaks tell the sounds apart
The whistle carries up to 5 km over ravines
The listener turns it back into Spanish

slides.question: After decades of decline, when did Silbo Gomero become a compulsory school subject on La Gomera?
slides.explanation: July 1999, in La Gomera’s primary and secondary schools. Ten years later, in 2009, UNESCO declared it a masterpiece of the intangible heritage of humanity.
